summary: Chinese framed adjectives/stative words become state events (have-mod-91 only frameless); quoted article titles as named publications; stronger whole-token/joined V+complement lookup and role traps; habitual narrowed to generic periodical activity; no node for 甚至/linking 还也/means verbs; general V+人/者 decomposition and 全/各 split; parts/content merged rule; compressions to stay under limit.

edits.old: Not events: entity nouns, property words used as plain modifiers,
edits.new: Not events: entity nouns, frameless modifiers (demonstratives, plain nouns),

edits.anchor: abstract predicates of 2.3 when there is no lexical verb.
edits.text: - Chinese adjectives and stative words that have a frame, predicative or attributive (with or without 的), are events: `(e / Adj-01 :ARG0 theme :aspect state)`, attributively `(n / N :ARG0-of (e / Adj-01 :aspect state))` (roles from the roleset); temporal `:overlap` with the governing event, `(author :full-affirmative e)`. `have-mod-91` only for a frameless property word.

edits.old: | X is Adj / X has property | `have-mod-91` |

edits.new:
- Use the most specific type: `newspaper` (报, 日报, 周报, tabloid), `magazine` (杂志/期刊), `book`, `program`, ...; `publication` only when the kind is unknown.
- A quoted article title or headline (「 」 or quotes) counted with 篇/则, in apposition to an article noun, or object of a publishing verb is `publication :name`: every word, bracket and punctuation mark an `:op`, the classifier on it, no inner nodes or triples; an article noun takes it as `:ARG1-of (i / identity-91 :ARG2 pub)`. Only direct content of a saying verb gets clause analysis and `:quote`.

edits.anchor: Never use a concept whose word is not a PropBank lemma unless it is `-00`.
edits.text: Look up V到/V出/V上 tokens whole first; when the complement is a separate token, also try the joined form and, if it has a frame, make one concept aligned to both tokens.

edits.old:
2. List all of its senses with their role descriptions. Do not stop at -01.
3. Choose the sense whose role descriptions match the participants in the sentence.
4. Copy the role numbers from that sense, not from -01 and not from English habit.
edits.new: 2. List all its senses with role descriptions (not only -01), choose the one matching the participants, and copy its role numbers (not from -01 or English habit).

edits.old: The belonging/membership sense of a verb is often not -01, and in it the owner is often `:ARG0` and the thing that belongs is `:ARG1`. A relative clause *the Y that belongs to X* then is `(y / Y :ARG0-of (b / V-0n :ARG1 x))` or `:ARG1-of`, whichever the frame gives the head noun; the owner fills the frame's owner role. Many Chinese intransitive and change-of-state verbs have only `:ARG0` (the thing that ceases, changes or acts). Do not default the theme to `:ARG1` by English habit. In particular, for change, become, reach and fall verbs (成, 达到, 跌, 变 type), the theme is usually `:ARG0` and the result or point reached is `:ARG1`. Copy the numbers from the roleset's role list every time. Traps: 有 has possession, existence/relationship-with and list-inclusion senses; count-as verbs (算是 type) number their roles from `:ARG0`. If the roleset lists only `:ARG0`, the single participant is `:ARG0` even when it looks like a patient (it starts, ceases, is founded, appears).
edits.new: Belonging senses are often not -01; there the owner is often `:ARG0` and the belonging thing `:ARG1` (a relative clause uses `:ARG0-of`/`:ARG1-of` as the frame gives the head noun). Many intransitive, change-of-state, become, reach, fall and be-elected verbs (成, 达到, 跌, 变 type) take the theme as `:ARG0` (result `:ARG1`); if the roleset lists only `:ARG0`, the single participant is `:ARG0` even when it looks like a patient. Traps: 有 has possession, existence/relationship-with, described-as-having (ability, feature) and list-inclusion senses; count-as verbs (算是) number from `:ARG0`; publishing/posting verbs usually make the place published in a numbered argument (not `:place`).

edits.old: A compound agent noun (V + 人/者, e.g. a founder or initiator) is decomposed: `(p / 人 :ARG0-of (v / V-01 :aspect performance))`, placed where the role noun goes (e.g. under `:ARG3` of the role predicate).
edits.new: A compound V + 人/者 noun is decomposed wherever it occurs: agent `(p / 人 :ARG0-of (v / V-01))` (`:aspect performance` when it is a role noun under `:ARG3`), patient `(p / 人 :ARG1-of (v / V-01 :aspect process))`. 全/各 + noun is noun `:mod 全`.

edits.old: - **Unexpressed participants.** Do not fill a roleset slot with a participant the text does not express. Re-enter a node only when the text itself expresses that participant in that role. The same holds for non-core relations (`:part-of`, `:possessor`, `:mod`, ...): add one only when a word or construction expresses it, not when it is merely implied. A subject grammatically shared through a control or means frame (以 X 而 Y, *known for doing X*, *try to X*) counts as expressed: re-enter it as the subject of the embedded verb too. Do not re-enter the subject into 为/为了-purpose clauses or into relative clauses; leave those roles out unless a word fills them.
edits.new: - **Unexpressed participants.** Fill a role (core, or `:part-of`, `:possessor`, `:mod`, ...) and re-enter a node only when a word or construction expresses that participant in that role, not when merely implied. A subject shared through a control or means frame (以 X 而 Y, *known for doing X*, *try to X*) counts as expressed: re-enter it in the embedded verb. Do not re-enter the subject into 为/为了-purpose clauses or relative clauses unless a word fills the role.

edits.old: - **Parts and media.** A physical edition or part of a publication is `:part-of` it, not `:possessor`. A medium noun (TV, 网络) modifying a program or product is `:medium`.
edits.new: - **Parts, content and media.** An edition, section, format or layout noun, or an article or content item, of a publication is `:part-of` it (never `:possessor`, never inverse `:part`). As a verb's argument the part noun is the argument, even when the publication name is the head after 的 (V了 A的《X》 → `:ARG1 (a / A :part-of x)`). A medium noun (TV, 网络) modifying a program or product is `:medium`.

edits.old: - **Formats and parts as arguments.** When a format, layout or section noun (版面, edition, section) of a publication is an argument of any verb, that noun is the argument and the publication is its `:part-of`. Never write the inverse `:part` on the whole. This holds even when the publication's name is the grammatical head after 的 (V了 A的《X》 → `:ARG1 (a / A :part-of x)`).

- **Repeated activity of an institution or periodical** (publishing, broadcasting, reporting, what it regularly contains or covers) is `habitual`, even with 了 and also as an event nominal (overrides `process`).
edits.new: - **Generic regular activity of an institution or periodical** (what it publishes, broadcasts or covers in general) is `habitual`, even with 了 and as an event nominal (overrides `process`). A single act about one specific item or occasion is `performance` when completed, even with a publication as agent.

edits.old: Focus particles 就, 便 get no node.
edits.new:
Focus particles 就, 便 and 甚至 (*even*) get no node, nor does 还/也 that only links a clause to an earlier clause or sentence (`:mod` only when it scopes inside one clause).
- A means verb (靠, 凭, 借 X 而/to Y) gets no node: X's event is the `:reason` of Y.
This covers subordinate, complement, coordinated and cause clauses, relative-clause verbs, event nominals, negated events and events in noun-phrase modifiers.

edits.old: Exception: when the negation is fused into one verb word (未经 type), write no `:polarity -`. The concept is the verb part without the negator, with its own PropBank sense and roles. Do not create a `-00` concept spelled with the negator.
edits.new: Fused negation (未经 type): no `:polarity -`; the concept is the verb without the negator, with its own sense and roles (no `-00` spelled with the negator).
